Six months after the market incident, Rachel received a call from Lily’s school.

Someone had attempted to pick her up.

A woman.

Not Marissa.

Aunt Carol.

Rachel drove there shaking.

Carol sat in the office.

“I wanted to see my granddaughter.”

“She’s your great-niece.”

“You know what I mean.”

“No.”

Rachel’s voice hardened.

“I know exactly what words mean now.”

Carol claimed she wanted to take Lily for ice cream.

Lily refused to leave the classroom.

Because Rachel had created a new rule.

Nobody picks you up unless Mom tells you personally.

Not a relative.

Not a friend.

Nobody.

Carol called the rule paranoid.

The school called it authorized pickup policy.

I liked the school’s wording better.

Rachel asked:

“Why would you think this was okay?”

Carol cried.

“Marissa misses her.”

There it was.

Not Lily misses Marissa.

Marissa misses Lily.

Adult feelings placed ahead of child safety.

Again.

Rachel had Carol removed from the pickup list permanently.

Then sent one message:

Do not contact Lily without my permission again.

Carol replied:

You’re destroying this family.

Rachel showed me.

Then deleted it.

“I used to be afraid people would think I was cruel.”

“What changed?”

She looked toward Lily doing homework.

“I became more afraid my daughter would think I wouldn't protect her because someone might call me cruel.”

That was growth.

Not dramatic.

Not cinematic.

Real.
